rules.title: Rules
rules.intro: How a campaign works, and how the winner is found.
rules.loggingBody: A campaign runs between two dates. Each day you fill in what you did: steps you walked, or kilometres you cycled. That is all there is to it.
rules.loggingLate: Forgot a day? You can fill it in later, as long as the campaign is still running. When it ends, the entries are locked. If something is properly wrong after that, an administrator can reopen the campaign so it can be put right.
rules.stepBody: There are two boxes to fill in.
rules.stepFieldStepsBody: What your phone or your watch counted.
rules.stepFieldCalculatedBody: Everything else. A swim, a game of badminton, an hour on the bike. None of that shows up as steps, so you convert it instead.
rules.stepCalculator: The calculator underneath your days does the converting. Pick the activity, roughly how hard it felt, and how many minutes it took.
rules.winnerLead: A step campaign is a prize draw, not a race.
rules.winnerTickets: Every 10,000 steps you log earns you a ticket. Log anything at all and you get at least one, so everybody taking part is in the draw.
rules.winnerDraw: When the campaign is over, a captain draws a ticket, and whoever holds it wins. More steps means more tickets and a better chance, but being top of the leaderboard does not win it on its own.
rules.winnerOnce: The draw happens once and the result is kept. Correcting an entry afterwards does not change who won.
rules.bikeLead: These are decided by days out, not by distance.
rules.bikeBody: How far you live from work is not an achievement, so the leaderboard counts the days you actually cycled rather than the kilometres. The distance is still shown. It just does not decide the order.
rules.bikeZero: A day counts when you actually rode. Writing a zero does not count.
rules.numbersBody: The MET values behind the calculator come from the 2024 Adult Compendium of Physical Activities. The sum it does is steps = minutes × MET ÷ 0.065.
rules.numbersEstimate: It is an estimate rather than a measurement. It does not know your weight, or how hard you were really going.
rules.numbersPadel: Padel is not listed in the compendium at all. We use a value from the range people report for it, 4 to 7 depending on effort.
